items.title: Section: Rāhula's Patient Path to Arhatship, and the Opening Definition of "Sense-Field"

items.zh: 界事善巧，如蘊善巧，亦應宣說嗢拕南頌。如界善巧，處事善巧嗢拕南頌，當知亦爾。云何眼處？謂若眼，已得不捨，於無間體非斷滅法。如眼處相，餘處自性，當知亦爾。
items.en: Regarding the skilful understanding of the elements, just as with the skilful understanding of the aggregates, a summary verse should likewise be spoken. As with the elements' own summary verse, so too should the sense-fields' own summary verse be understood. What is the eye sense-field? That which, once the eye has been attained and not abandoned, continues uninterrupted, not being a soon-to-cease phenomenon. As with the characteristics of the eye sense-field, so too should the essential nature of the remaining sense-fields be understood.

items.title: Section: Sense-Field Versus Field-of-Contact, and the Four Ways an Eye May or May Not Be a "Sense-Field"

items.zh: 問：處、觸處，何差別？答：處如前說。觸處者，謂與觸俱，或能無間引發諸觸、隨順於觸所有諸處。問：若眼亦處耶？設處亦眼耶？答：有眼非處；謂若眼，已得不捨，然是無間斷滅之法。有處非眼；謂所餘處安住處相。有亦眼亦處；謂若眼，已得不捨，亦非無間斷滅之法。有非眼非處；謂若眼，不得，或得已捨，及餘耳等不住處相。
items.en: Question: what is the difference between a sense-field and a field-of-contact? Answer: a sense-field is as defined above. A field-of-contact is any sense-field that operates together with contact, or that can immediately give rise to the various contacts and accords with contact. Question: is every eye a sense-field? Is every sense-field an eye? Answer: there is an eye that is not a sense-field — an eye attained and not abandoned, yet which is a soon-to-cease phenomenon. There is a sense-field that is not an eye — any of the remaining sense-fields abiding in the nature of a sense-field. There is something both eye and sense-field — an eye attained, not abandoned, and not a soon-to-cease phenomenon. There is something neither eye nor sense-field — an eye not attained, or attained and then abandoned, together with the remaining faculties not abiding in the nature of a sense-field.

items.title: Section: Six Meanings of "Sense-Field," and the Three Conditions It Exists to Reveal

items.zh: 問：若處亦觸處耶？設觸處亦處耶？答：諸觸處必是處，有處非觸處。謂眼等不與觸合，亦復不能引無間觸，然非無間斷滅之法。若於色界或生或長所有鼻、舌，若生無想有情天中所有諸根，於一切時當知必定非處。問：處名何義？為顯何義建立處耶？答：諸心心所生長門義、緣義、方便義、和合性義、所依止義、居住處義，是名處義。為欲顯示等無間、所緣、增上三種緣義，故建立處。
items.en: Question: is every sense-field a field-of-contact? Is every field-of-contact a sense-field? Answer: every field-of-contact is necessarily a sense-field, but there is a sense-field that is not a field-of-contact — the eye and the rest not meeting contact, nor able to give rise to uninterrupted contact, yet still not a soon-to-cease phenomenon. The nose and tongue of one born or matured in the form realm, and all the faculties of one born in the mindless heaven, should be understood as never, at any time, being a genuine field-of-contact. Question: what is the meaning of the term "sense-field"? For what purpose is the category of sense-field established? Answer: the meaning of "sense-field" is the gateway through which mind and mental factors grow; the condition they depend on; the preparatory means of their arising; that which, combined with its object, generates contact; that which mind and mental factors constantly rely on; and the dwelling-place they abide in. It is in order to reveal the three kinds of condition — the immediately-preceding condition, the object-condition, and the dominant condition — that the category of sense-field is established.

items.title: Section: The Sense-Fields Complete — Meditative Attainments Folded In, and the Same Dependency as the Elements

items.zh: 廣分別處及次第，隨其所應，如界當知。又世尊言：有八勝處。廣說如經。如是十遍處。又有四處，謂空無邊處等。又有二處，謂無想處、非想非非想處。如是等法處名說者，如所說相，隨其所應，當知皆在十二處攝。又處依止，如界應知。
items.en: The extensive analysis of the sense-fields, and the reasoning behind their sequence, should be understood by analogy with the elements, according to what applies. The Blessed One also spoke of the eight bases of mastery, as extensively explained in the sūtras, and likewise the ten meditative totalities. There are also the four formless bases, beginning with the sphere of infinite space. There is also the twofold grouping of the mindless attainment and the state of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. All such things called "sense-field," according to their respective characteristics, should be understood to be entirely subsumed within the twelve sense-fields. The sense-fields' own dependency should likewise be understood as with the elements.

items.title: Section: A Fourth Skilful Understanding Opens — What Dependent Origination Actually Says About the Self

items.zh: 復次，云何名緣生法？謂無主宰、無有作者、無有受者、無自作用，不得自在，從因而生，託眾緣轉，本無而有，有已散滅。唯法所顯、唯法能潤、唯法所潤，墮在相續，如是等相名緣生法。
items.en: Next, what is called a dependently arisen phenomenon? That which has no ruling self, no agent, no recipient, no real independent function, and no autonomy whatsoever — arising from causes, relying on a gathering of conditions, originally nonexistent, then existent, and, once existent, ultimately dispersing. That which is manifested purely as phenomena, in which phenomena alone are what nourish and phenomena alone are what is nourished, and which falls into a continuing succession — characteristics such as these are what is called dependently arisen phenomena.

items.title: Section: Cause-Aspect and Effect-Aspect, Real and Provisional Among the Twelve Links

items.zh: 當知此中，因名緣起，果名緣生。此無明隨眠不斷有故，彼無明纏有；此無明纏生故，彼諸行轉。如是諸行種子不斷故，諸行得生；諸行生故，得有識轉。如是所餘諸緣起支流轉道理，如其所應，當知亦爾。當知有、生及老死支，是假有法；所餘有支，是實有法。復由五相建立緣起差別。何等為五？一、眾苦引因依處，二、眾苦生因依處，三、眾苦引因，四、眾苦生因，五、眾苦生起。眾苦引因依處者，謂於現法中，名色為緣六處生起，不斷不知。此為所緣及依處故，一切愚夫於內自體愚癡生起，是名無明。
items.en: It should be understood that, within this chain, cause is called dependent origination, and effect is called dependently arisen phenomena. Because ignorance's latent tendency remains unbroken, ignorance's active manifestation comes to exist; because that manifestation of ignorance arises, the formations dependent on it become active. Likewise, because the seeds of the formations remain unbroken, the formations arise; because the formations arise, consciousness becomes active. The remaining links of dependent origination should be understood by the same principle of arising, according to what applies. It should be understood that existence, birth, and old-age-and-death are provisionally existent phenomena; the remaining links are truly existent phenomena. Dependent origination's own distinctions are further established by five aspects. What are the five? First, the basis for the drawing-cause of suffering; second, the basis for the generating-cause of suffering; third, the drawing-cause of suffering itself; fourth, the generating-cause of suffering itself; fifth, the very arising of suffering. The basis for the drawing-cause of suffering is this: in the present life, name-and-form conditions the arising of the six sense-fields, unbroken and unknown. Because this serves as object and basis, every foolish, unlearned being gives rise to ignorant clinging to an inner self — this is called ignorance.

items.zh: 無明緣故，次後諸行，乃至後時有觸緣受。此中六處，名無明等引因依處。

items.title: Section: Completing the Fivefold Suffering-Cause Framework — Why Birth and Old Age Deserve the Name "Suffering"

items.zh: 眾苦生因依處者，謂諸愚夫觸為緣故，於現法中諸受生起；此為依處，於外境界發起諸愛；由愛為緣，次後有取；取為緣故，次後有有。如是愛等三種生因，用觸緣受為所依處。眾苦引因者，謂無明緣行，乃至觸緣受。現法中識，為福非福及不動業之所熏習，後後種子之所隨逐，能引當來餘身識等生、老死苦，是故說此為彼引因。眾苦生因者，謂受緣愛、愛緣取、取緣有，是名當來眾苦生因。即先所作業為煩惱攝受，未來世生將現前故，當知名有。眾苦生起者，謂有緣生、生緣老死，如是名為眾苦生起。即識、名色、六處、觸、受先種子性，隨所依時，曾得眾苦引因之名；今已與果，名生、老死，復得苦名。
items.en: The basis for the generating-cause of suffering is this: unlearned beings, through contact as condition, give rise to feelings in the present life; relying on this basis, craving for external objects arises; craving conditions grasping; grasping conditions existence. Thus craving and the rest, these three generating-causes, take contact conditioning feeling as their basis. The drawing-cause of suffering is ignorance conditioning formations, through contact conditioning feeling. Consciousness in the present life, permeated by wholesome, unwholesome, and unshakeable karma, is followed by successive seeds able to draw forth the consciousness and the rest of a future, other body, and hence birth and old-age-death suffering — this is why these are called its drawing-cause. The generating-cause of suffering is feeling conditioning craving, craving conditioning grasping, grasping conditioning existence — this is called the generating-cause of future suffering. The very karma previously created, now taken hold of by affliction, about to manifest as a future life, should be understood as "existence." The arising of suffering is existence conditioning birth, birth conditioning old age and death — this is called the arising of suffering. Consciousness, name-and-form, the six sense-fields, contact, and feeling, while still in the nature of seeds, at the time of their dependence, once received the name "drawing-cause of suffering"; now, having yielded their result, they are named birth and old age-death, and further receive the name "suffering."

blocks.text: The twelve sense-fields, and then a new topic: dependent origination, examined with the same precision.
An eye attained, not abandoned, and whose next moment does not cease. Master Cháng Bǎi: the eye is present, not lost, its continuity unbroken: a gate for consciousness.
Master Cháng Bǎi: an eye that cannot give rise to a next moment of eye is not called a sense-field. "Field of contact" here refers to the mental factor of contact.
The mental field reveals the condition of immediate succession; the object fields, the object condition; the faculty fields, the dominant condition.
Whatever is called a "field" falls within the twelve.
Master Cháng Bǎi: dependently arisen things are bound by conditions and have no freedom; this refutes those who say things are made by a creator.
Existence, birth, and ageing-death are provisional; the rest are real. Master Cháng Bǎi: "existence" is set upon the combined seeds of six links, formations through feeling.
Master Cháng Bǎi: this draws forth a future ripened body, and so the suffering of birth and ageing-death.
"Bound by conditions, without freedom." This is the heart of dependent origination: nothing in the chain acts on its own.

options: all form seen by the eye, past and future included, sense-field being all objects, unrelated to the faculty
eye-consciousness itself
the seed of the eye
the eye attained and not abandoned, whose next moment is not a ceasing phenomenon
quiz.why: The treatise defines the eye sense-field as an eye attained, not abandoned, and whose next moment does not cease. Master Cháng Bǎi: the eye is manifest, not lost, and its continuity unbroken, a gate for consciousness; 處 means giving growth, so only an eye that can give rise to a next eye is called a sense-field.

quiz.q: The English has "a not-yet-ceased phenomenon" and "a soon-to-cease phenomenon." What is the problem?
options: no problem: "not-yet-ceased" means still alive, the treatise saying a living person's eye is a sense-field, unrelated to the next moment
非斷滅法 means an eternal eye, and should be "eternal"
無間斷滅 means unbroken, and should be "unbroken"
the point is whether the next moment continues; a last eye ceases next and so is no sense-field; "not-yet-ceased" loses this
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the eye is not destroyed, but cannot continue uninterrupted, and in the next moment it ceases; it cannot be called a sense-field because it cannot give rise to a next moment of eye. So the test is the immediately next moment. "Soon-to-cease" comes close, but "not-yet-ceased" misses it, since a last eye too has not yet ceased.

quiz.q: The English has "the feelings that contact brings about" for 諸觸. What is the problem?
options: 諸觸 are the body's cold, heat, softness, and hardness, so "feelings" is apt, meaning bodily sensation, unrelated to factors
諸觸 means sexual contact
諸觸 means meeting people
諸觸 are pleasant, painful, and neutral contact, the mental factor; the English changes this to "feelings," confusing contact with feeling
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 觸處 here refers to the mental factor contact, not the object of the body faculty; 諸觸 are painful, pleasant, and neutral contacts. So the sentence stays with contact throughout. The English "feelings" moves a step along the chain, to what contact produces.

quiz.q: What does sense-field mean, and for what purpose is it established?
options: cause, seed, nature, lineage, subtlety, sustaining; to reveal causal relation and use, the same as elements
the gateway of growth, condition, means, combination, support, and dwelling; to reveal the three conditions of succession, object, and dominance
accumulation and intermixture; to reveal selflessness
dwelling and lodging; to reveal the monastic retreat
quiz.why: The treatise gives six meanings and says sense-fields are established to reveal three conditions. Master Cháng Bǎi: the condition of immediate succession is the mental sense-field; the object condition is the outer six; the dominant condition is the inner six. Elements, by contrast, reveal the causal condition, so the two lists complement each other.

quiz.q: Why are the eight masteries, ten totalities, and four formless bases all within the twelve?
options: because they are all form, under the form sense-field, so the twelve suffice, unrelated to mind
they depend on mind, mind being the mental sense-field and its objects the mental-object field, so they stay within the twelve
because the sūtras happen to say so
they in fact lie outside the twelve
quiz.why: The treatise says all such things called 處 are subsumed within the twelve. Master Cháng Bǎi: these depend on mind; mind belongs to the mental sense-field and its objects to the mental-object field, and so none exceeds the twelve. Aggregates, elements, and sense-fields speak of one world of body and mind from different angles. The English "meditative mastery" hides the word 處.

quiz.q: What is a dependently arisen phenomenon, and what marks does the treatise list?
options: having a ruler, agent, and recipient; self-producing and unchanging, needing no conditions, whence the name
created by the Buddha and upheld by disciples
existing only in the desire realm
no ruler, agent, recipient, own function, or freedom; from causes, by conditions; once absent, now existing, then dispersing
quiz.why: The treatise lists these marks of a dependently arisen phenomenon. Master Cháng Bǎi: dependently arisen phenomena are bound by conditions and have no freedom, which refutes outsiders who say things are natural; dependent origination is principle, and dependently arisen phenomena are fact, neither one nor different. The English "no real independent function" is well judged.

quiz.q: The English has "nourished ... by other phenomena, ... purely nourishes" for 唯法能潤、唯法所潤. What is the problem with the order?
options: no problem: the order makes no difference, both being one link, whatever the matching
what nourishes is ignorance, what is nourished formations
the English swaps 能潤 and 所潤; what nourishes is craving and grasping, what is nourished is existence, so matching links goes wrong
what nourishes is birth, what is nourished ageing and death
quiz.why: The Sub-commentary maps the four: ignorance through feeling are manifested; craving and grasping nourish; existence is nourished; birth and ageing-death fall into succession. Master Cháng Bǎi: craving and grasping moisten the seeds of formations through feeling and so accomplish existence. The English puts "nourished" first, which breaks this ordered mapping to the links.

quiz.q: Which of the twelve links are provisional, and why?
options: ignorance, formations, and consciousness, being mental, without substance, only form being real
all twelve are real
existence, birth, and ageing-death; existence is set on six links' seeds, and birth and ageing-death are phases of manifestation
all twelve are provisional
quiz.why: The treatise says existence, birth, and ageing-death are provisional and the rest real. Master Cháng Bǎi: existence is established on the combined seeds of six links, formations through feeling; birth and ageing-death are differences of phase in the manifestation of consciousness through feeling. So these three have no substance apart from those.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi say of "unbroken and unknown" in the basis of the drawing-cause?
options: unbroken means undamaged faculties; unknown means illiteracy, so ignorance is a matter of schooling, cured by learning letters
the six fields are followed by seeds of affliction, heaviness not severed; not truly penetrating their own marks is unknown
unbroken means continuing life; unknown means not knowing one's date of death
unbroken means continuing good; unknown means not knowing good
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the six sense-fields are followed by seeds of affliction such as ignorance, and heaviness not yet severed is "unbroken"; not truly penetrating their marks is "unknown." Note the English "ignorant clinging" adds grasping to 愚癡, though the treatise will shortly separate ignorance from view.

quiz.q: The English has "future bodily consciousness and the rest" for 當來餘身識等. What is wrong?
options: 餘身 is another life's body, the consciousness of a future body, not body-consciousness; five seeds manifest as birth and ageing-death
餘身識 is the fifth, body-consciousness, so the English is right, meaning future touch, unrelated to the next life
餘身 means what remains of the body
餘身 means another person's body
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this can draw forth a future ripened body, that is, the manifestation of the five seeds of consciousness through feeling, and hence the suffering of birth and ageing-death. So 餘身 means another body. The English text reads "bodily consciousness," which suggests the fifth consciousness, although its own overview has "a future body's consciousness."
